title: Agent-in-the-loop to distill expert knowledge into artificial intelligence models: a survey
authors: Gao, J.; Zhang, Y.; Chen, Y.; Dong, Y.; Chen, Y.; Song, S.; Tang, B.; Gu, Y.
tldr: Surveys Agent-in-the-Loop ML (AIL-ML) where humans and large models collaborate to construct domain-specific AI with lower costs and enhanced expert knowledge integration.
problem_and_motivation: Large neural networks excel in general domains but struggle in expert knowledge areas (healthcare, law) due to data sparsity and high annotation costs. Human-in-the-loop ML addresses this but overlooked the potential of large models as human proxies.
approach: Conducted an extensive literature survey of works from top CS and HCI conferences (2018-2024) plus arXiv (2023-2024).
Proposes the AIL-ML framework unifying Human-in-the-Loop (HIL-ML) and Large-Model-in-the-Loop (LMIL-ML).
Categorizes methods by data processing stage: data collection, initialization, quality enhancement, annotation, and model development stages.
Provides formal mathematical descriptions for each AIL-ML category including data-level and model-level agent interventions.
Reviews applications in expert domains and discusses future research directions.
findings: AIL-ML combines human intuition and expertise with large model computational power and reasoning.
LMIL-ML reduces reliance on human annotation by using large models as proxies in the modeling loop.
Existing HIL-ML surveys fail to address the role of large models as participants in the loop.
Agent interventions span data acquisition, processing, model development, and optimization stages.
AIL-ML improves model accuracy, adaptability, explainability, and reduces privacy risks in expert domains.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Provides the first comprehensive survey of Agent-in-the-Loop ML, unifying human and large model participation in a single framework. Formalizes a taxonomy of intervention methods across the ML pipeline. Highlights the underexplored role of large models as active participants rather than passive tools in the ML loop.
directly_justifies: Large models can serve as human proxies in expert domain ML tasks.
AIL-ML reduces annotation costs while improving model accuracy.
Agent interventions span all stages from data to model optimization.
limits: Survey paper without empirical validation of the proposed framework.
Financial applications of AIL-ML are not specifically addressed.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematically scanned all topic domains (1.A-14.C). Assigned 14.B medium relevance for ML deployment discussion. Assigned 5.C and 7.A low for potential cross-domain applicability. Rejected most personal finance-specific topics (1.A-4.C, 6.A-13.C) as the paper surveys general ML methodology for expert domains.
